title: real-world-claim-mapping-and-sample-scripts
content:
TL;DR: working brief to translate our latency + cost technical advantages into persona-specific claims, microproofs (what evidence to show), and short conversational scripts field teams can use. This is intentionally pragmatic: give reps and PMs concrete 1–2 line claims + linked artifacts they can attach to proposals or customer calls.

Context and goal:
- Problem: customers understand latency and cost matter but ask for exact numbers and proof. Sales needs crisp claims that map to artifacts engineering owns.
- Goal: produce a small claim library (3 prioritized claims), a matrix mapping each claim to evidence artifacts (benchmarks, logs, customer examples), rebuttals to common objections, and 10 quick scripts for demo/SDR/rev ops.

Target personas (what they care about):
- Product/Platform Engineer (latency, jitter, deterministic tail behavior, integration complexity)
- ML Engineer/Model Ops (throughput, model variants, quantization support, KV cache behavior)
- Infra/Cloud Architecture (predictable capacity, autoscaling costs, burst behavior)
- Procurement/Finance (unit economics: cost per 1M tokens, committed vs variable spend)

Primary claims (short, attributable, prioritized):
1) Faster p95 production latency on common gen workloads vs hosted alternatives.
   - Claim line: "In real workloads our p95 generation latency is typically 30–60% lower than comparable hosted endpoints at equivalent model sizes."
   - Microproofs/evidence: perf-benchmarks repo (latency/p95 runs), customer A telemetry (anonymized p95 traces), side-by-side trace screenshot (console: trace-id).
   - Metric threshold to use externally: safe claim = "up to 60% lower p95" with the qualifier "on comparable model size and sequence length; see methodology."

2) Lower per-token inference cost at scale through workload-aware batching + KV caching.
   - Claim line: "For busy conversational workloads we cut per-token spend by 25–45% compared to naïve hosted endpoints through batching + prefix caching optimizations."
   - Microproofs/evidence: Optimize-reports (recommendations -> simulated savings), Dedicated customer invoice comparison (committed capacity vs consumption), sample cost model spreadsheet (1M messages, avg tokens).
   - Metric threshold to use externally: "typical savings 25–45%" with note about workload dependency.

3) Predictable tail-latency SLOs with graceful fallbacks.
   - Claim line: "We provide SLA-backed latency tiers and automated fallback policies so apps stay within latency targets during spikes."
   - Microproofs/evidence: SLA doc excerpt, rollout policy config yaml (console screenshots), incident playbook examples where fallbacks kept app within SLO.
   - External phrasing: emphasize reliability and predictable latency, avoid exact SLA numbers without legal review.

Mapping claims to artifacts (microproof map) - what to attach in a customer deck or email:
- Latency claim -> perf-benchmarks/p95-report.pdf; customer p95 traces (redacted); console latency dashboard screenshot; short note on model variant used (e.g., redwood-13b-quant).
- Cost claim -> cost-model-1m-tokens.xlsx (sheet exported as CSV text), optimize-run-simulation.md, Dedicated billing sample (redacted).
- SLO/fallback claim -> sla-summary.pdf, rollout-policy-sample.png, incident-after-action-summary-2024-11.pdf.

Competitive angle / talking points vs typical opponents (concise):
- Versus large public-hosted API providers: "They may have scale but we optimize the per-request path for production inference (KV caching, continuous batching) which reduces both tail latency and unit cost for real workloads."
- Versus self-hosted runtimes / OSS: "Self-hosted can be cheaper on raw hardware but requires ops time and tuning; our Dedicated offering gives similar economics with predictable throughput and operational SLAs."
- Versus other inference vendors who emphasize single benchmark numbers: "Benchmarks matter, but per-workload economics diverge. We show workload-specific simulations and real-customer billing comparisons, not just synthetic FLOPS numbers."

Common objections + rebuttals (field-ready):
- Objection: "Benchmarks are synthetic, not our workload."
  - Rebuttal: "We get that — we’ll run a quick 48-hour trial with your sample traffic and show concrete p95 & cost delta. We can also provide a tailored cost simulation from your logs."
- Objection: "How do you compare to X provider's newest model?"
  - Rebuttal: "We compare by model class and sequence distribution. If you give us a model/seq-length distribution, we’ll run the same model/variant and show the delta on your workload."
- Objection: "Savings sound optimistic."
  - Rebuttal: "We provide the simulation spreadsheet and the exact inputs; you can validate — and we’ll provide a second opinion via a small Dedicated pilot."

Suggested external phrasing rules (marketing/legal guardrails):
- Use ranges (e.g., 25–45%) not point estimates.
- Always append the qualifier: "on representative conversational workloads; results depend on sequence lengths and model family."
- Any claim with a specific competitor name or absolute percent must be signed off by legal/marketing.

Field assets / ready-to-use scripts (10 short scripts). These are one-liners + 1 follow-up sentence you can copy to Slack/email/demo notes.
1) SDR opening (email subject): "Reduce inference spend without sacrificing latency — quick question"
   Body: "We’ve helped similar teams cut per-token inference costs by ~30% using batching + prefix caching on live traffic. Do you have 10 minutes to see a short simulation with your numbers?"
2) AE demo opener (voice): "We’ll show a direct comparison: same model family, same request shape. First we’ll run a 5-min live sample to show p95 and cost estimate."
3) Infra partner (voice): "We design Dedicated pools to keep burst costs predictable; think of it like reserved instances but tuned to inference scaling patterns."
4) ML Eng rebuttal: "Our runtime supports quantized kernels and KV cache semantics that keep generation quality while lowering cost — we can show sample outputs if you want to compare."
5) Procurement email: "Attached is a one-page unit-econ sheet showing expected monthly spend across three traffic tiers; we can turn this into a contract appendix."
6) Customer success check-in: "Since onboarding we’ve seen p95 latency improve and per-token billing align with the model we projected; pulling the last 30 days of telemetry now."
7) Slide headline for execs: "Predictable inference economics: lower unit cost, stable latency, fewer incidents."
8) Cold outreach (concise): "Curious how your models would behave under batch+cache optimizations? 15-min audit = tailored cost estimate."
9) Field quote for case study: "Cutting tail latency and cost let us deliver richer features without ballooning infra spend."
10) Partner pitch (brief): "Bundle our runtime with your deployment orchestration and offer customers a single bill for inference SLA + infra."

Example microproof snippet to paste in proposals (1-paragraph):
"In a production conversational workload modeled on 3k concurrent sessions (avg 200 tokens/session), Redwood’s continuous batching + KV caching reduced token generation time p95 by ~45% and produced 32% lower per-token spend in our simulated billing model. Attach: perf-benchmarks/3k-concurrent-report.pdf and cost-model-3k.csv (redacted)."

Quick methodology note (for engineering):
- Repro steps for perf claim: run perf-benchmarks/runner with same model family and sequence length distribution; compare p50/p95/p99; run with/without KV caching and continuous batching. Save console trace and annotate trace-ids in the notebook.
- Cost sim: use cost-model template, plug in billing rates (hosted vs dedicated), token distribution, and request concurrency.

Sample evidence checklist before enabling a claim externally:
- Have matching benchmark artifacts (pdf/png) uploaded to the perf-benchmarks repo + share link.
- Redacted customer telemetry or trial data OR simulation outputs using customer traffic.
- Legal review for any named-competitor comparisons.
- Marketing approval for slides/external messaging.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we want a canonical external-facing number for "typical savings" (e.g., promote 30% as the headline) or keep to ranges (25–45%)? (Marketing + data team decision).
- Should sales be permitted to promise a trial that includes a free Dedicated pilot? (Pricing/legal).
- Who owns the canonical benchmark artifacts folder and the authority to sign claims (prod-bench leads)?

Next steps (owners):
- Aisha: assemble a one-page claim sheet with three claims + 2-slide proof snippets (due 2025-03-07).
- Miguel: export canonical p95 and cost PDFs from perf-benchmarks and add trace annotations (due 2025-03-05).
- Claire: coordinate legal sign-off and produce a short guidance note on competitor mentions (due 2025-03-10).
- Ethan: build a lightweight trial intake form that attaches a 48-hour trial runner to the RL engine (JIRA-3890) (due 2025-03-12).

Notes to self / working items (rough):
- Keep claim language modular so a) SDRs can use one-liners b) AEs can expand with the microproofs.
- Create a one-click bundle in the Console to export the 3 claim artifacts (latency PDF, cost CSV, policy screenshot).

Appendix: files to create and where to put them (working):
- perf-benchmarks/claim-library/p95-claims-2025-03.pdf
- sales-assets/one-pager-claims-v1.pdf
- optimize/cost-sim-templates/1m-10m-100m.csv
- console/screenshots/fallback-policy-2025-02-20.png

End.
